description: A page of the city's daily paper, printed in the last weeks before the presses stopped.  The headlines grow shorter and more frantic with every issue.
A mimeographed notice from the ward People's Committee, the kind pasted on lamp posts and read aloud over the loa phường.
A note on a scrap of paper, the ink blurred by humidity.
A dog-eared volume of a serialized martial-arts epic, translated from Chinese and rented by the day from the book stall at the end of the hẻm.  Heroes, sects, poisoned needles and secret manuals.

snippet_category.text: This is volume 7 of "The Sword of the Nine Rivers".  The hero has just learned that his master was the villain all along, again.
This is volume 2 of "Legend of the Jade Phoenix Sect".  Someone has underlined every description of a secret technique.
This is volume 11 of "The Beggar King of the Southern Marshes".  The rental stamp inside says it was due back three weeks ago.

description: A small booklet of Buddhist sutras and daily chants, printed by a pagoda and given away free to worshippers.  The pages are soft from handling and smell of incense.

Lịch vạn niên: a perpetual lunar calendar with lucky and unlucky days, auspicious hours for weddings and funerals, zodiac readings and the dates of every festival.  Your grandmother never made a decision without it.

A thick laminated binder listing thousands of song numbers for a karaoke machine: bolero ballads, revolutionary songs, Hong Kong pop and a few English hits.  Flicking through it brings back loud, happy nights.
